query: What kinds of tickets create heavier agent workload?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing tickets by type is a core axis for grouping workload. Values are well-grounded in short_description (e.g., 'database', 'vpn_access'), though the intranet row mapped to 'network_wifi' is a slightly loose reading.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Failure mode gives a genuine new axis to relate ticket nature to workload. Values track the text well ('disconnection', 'no_access', 'intermittent'), with reasonable Unknown/NULL for silent rows.

per_column.name: affected_system_type
per_column.rationale: Useful but largely a deterministic restatement of incident_category (email->email_server, vpn->vpn_gateway), so it adds limited independent leverage. Values are reasonable inferences from the description.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Scope (single_user vs department_wide vs production_system) would strongly relate to workload, but short_descriptions rarely state scope. Labels like 'production_system' for 'Unable to access the database' are confident specifics not supported by the terse source text.

per_column.name: recurrence_pattern
per_column.rationale: Recurrence would be relevant to workload, but 'repeat_same_system' is asserted for rows whose text gives no recurrence signal (e.g., 'Unable to access the database'). This is an invented inference; only 'frequent'/'unstable' phrasing supports intermittent/repeat.

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket self-resolved is highly relevant to workload, but the source text (description + timestamps) does not indicate self-resolution; values like True for the intranet row are unsupported inferences.

per_column.name: requires_escalation
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (False for 400, NULL for 100, no True observed), so it provides almost no discriminating power for the query. It is not contradicted by text but carries no analytical leverage.

judge.rationale: The category/failure-mode columns provide genuine, well-grounded axes for analyzing which ticket kinds drive workload. However several columns (scope_indicator, recurrence_pattern, self_resolved) assert specifics the terse short_description cannot support, and requires_escalation is near-constant with little value. Overall the set is analytically relevant but groundedness is dragged down by confident inferences on silent rows.
